title: Music Form/Genre Headings: Medium of Performance
scope: Patterns for music form/genre headings that include medium of performance (parenthetical medium qualifiers, instrument-list headings, 'and'/'with' connectors, numbers in parentheses, vocal range, type of chorus, choral parts, ', Arranged', ', Unaccompanied'). Each entry states whether the sheet makes the construction free-floating or requires an authority record.
general_notes: A large number of music form/genre headings that include medium of performance have been established in the subject authority file. With some exceptions (see H 250 and below), authority records for these types of headings are no longer made because: 1) cross references are no longer required; 2) the order of musical instruments given in the headings has been a pattern for some time; and 3) the patterns the headings follow are amply illustrated in the authority file.

When specifying an instrument in a heading, use the form of name for the instrument established in the subject authority file. If the name of the instrument has not been established, make two proposals, one for the name of the instrument and the other for its music, which will authorize the instrument to be used in bibliographic records as a medium of performance.

Do not include more than 9 instruments or 9 soloists in a heading, counting all categories. If the solo group is larger than 9, use an appropriate heading that incorporates the term "ensemble" (cf. sec. 5).
For guidance on subdivisions for musical compositions, see H 1160.

entries.rule: Solo instruments in category order: (1) keyboard, (2) wind, (3) plucked or hammered stringed without keyboard, (4) percussion, electronic, and other, (5) bowed stringed, (6) unspecified, (7) continuo; alphabetical within each category except bowed strings in score order, high to low. Comma-separated; 3 to 9 instruments/soloists. First word capitalized, rest lowercase.
examples: Nonets (Bassoon, clarinet, flute, horn, oboe, violin, viola, cello, double bass)
Octets (Piano, clarinet, flute, guitar, mandolin, accordion, percussion, double bass)
String quintets (Violin, viola d'amore, viola, cello, violone)
Sextets (Piano, clarinet, flute, percussion, violin, cello)
exceptions: More than 9 instruments or soloists: use a heading with the term "ensemble" (sec. 5).
Do not use "and" between elements when three or more elements precede "with" or when there are more than two soloists (sec. 6.a).

entries.rule: Two solo instruments joined by "and"; order per sec. 2, but for Western music the chordal or accompanying instrument is second (sec. 3.c).
exceptions: Chordal (keyboard or plucked) or accompanying instrument goes in second position (sec. 3.c).

entries.rule: Create an authority record for the combination; reference from reverse order. Order per sec. 2; chordal or accompanying instrument second for Western music on Western instruments (optionally one Western and one non-Western instrument).
exceptions: Electronic and balloon music [reference, not authorized]
Flute and bassoon music [reference, not authorized]
Piano and trombone music [reference, not authorized]
Piano and mandolin music [reference, not authorized]

entries.rule: When one of two instruments is unspecified, establish the heading beginning with Duets; references from both other forms.
exceptions: Duets (Piano and unspecified instrument) [reference]
Piano and unspecified instrument music [reference]

entries.rule: Two or more parts for the same instrument, or for unspecified instruments, in a group with other solo instruments: plural name followed by arabic numeral in parentheses. No authority record necessary.
examples: String nonets (Violins (4), violas (2), cellos (2), double bass)
Septets (Organ (4 hands), horn, trombone, trumpets (2), tuba)
exceptions: Do not number percussion players (sec. 4.b(4)(b)).
Do not number electronics, Electronic music, or Computer music (sec. 4.b(5)).

entries.rule: Music for two of the same wind, plucked, bowed stringed, or keyboard instrument. The authority record then authorizes the modification in all pattern headings.
exceptions: Three or more keyboard instruments constitute an ensemble: [Instrument] ensembles / Keyboard instrument ensembles (sec. 4.b(2)(b)(ii)).

entries.pattern: [Instrument] music ([n] hands); in qualifiers: ([Instrument], [n] hands) when sole instrument, [instrument] ([n] hands) in a list
entries.rule: Exceptional number of hands (other than two) for an instrument; authority record for the music of the instrument with that number of hands. With more than one instrument, hands follow the number of instruments.
examples: Quintets (Piano (1 hand), clarinet, violin, viola, cello)
Septets (Organ (4 hands), horn, trombone, trumpets (2), tuba)
exceptions: Left-hand piano music [reference]
Right-hand piano music [reference]
Keyboard as accompaniment in vocal music headings: no parentheses, comma form: Songs (High voice) with piano, 4 hands; Choruses, Secular (Mixed voices) with piano, 4 hands.

entries.rule: One performer playing more than one of the same keyboard instrument; performer is the last element.

Established headings for 2 through 9 unspecified instruments; number of unspecified instruments indicated even when the heading begins with the number of players; the number is also given in related headings.

entries.pattern: [Form/genre heading] ([solo instrument(s)] with [accompanying instrument(s) or ensemble])
entries.rule: Accompaniment follows the connector "with" inside the qualifier. Solo instruments listed per sec. 2 / sec. 3. Ensemble term singular.
examples: Concertos (Piano, saxophone, double bass with instrumental ensemble)
Concertos (Bass clarinet and double bass with jazz ensemble)
exceptions: Full orchestra is assumed for concertos: Concertos (Clarinet), not Concertos (Clarinet with orchestra) (sec. 5.d).

entries.rule: An established ensemble term (singular) as the sole medium.
exceptions: Orchestra is not added to overtures, symphonic poems, symphonies (and as concerto accompaniment) when performed by full orchestra: Symphonic poems; Symphonies (sec. 5.d).
Concertos (Orchestra [Band, etc.]) only when the composer calls the work a concerto for the entire large ensemble; never for chamber music with one player to a part (sec. 5.e).

entries.pattern: [Form/genre heading] ([single instrument or electronics])  (non-orchestral medium for forms assuming orchestra)
entries.rule: When a form that assumes full orchestra is for another medium, include the medium.
Instrument-list heading (no form term) followed by "with" and the accompanying ensemble. Two soloists joined by "and"; three or more by commas with no "and".
examples: Clarinet, flute, violin, cello with chamber orchestra
Piano, horn, glockenspiel, xylophone with orchestra
Pianos (2), celesta, percussion, synthesizer with chamber orchestra
Guitar and piano with jazz ensemble
Saxophone and guitar with jazz ensemble
Electronics and piano with percussion ensemble
Clarinet, flute, violin, cello with instrumental ensemble

entries.rule: Free-floating with form/genre headings for arranged instrumental music; follows any closing parenthesis.
exceptions: Larger vocal forms and instrumental forms that do not indicate medium: not free-floating; must be established, e.g. Operas, Arranged; Oratorios, Arranged; Motion picture music, Arranged; Incidental music, Arranged (sec. 7.b).
Never with forms usually qualified by type of chorus: Cantatas; Masses; Choruses; Requiems (sec. 7.b).
Never with works for solo singers or one singer to a part: Sacred vocal duets [trios, etc.]; Songs; Sacred songs; Vocal duets [trios, etc.]; Solo cantatas; Vocalises (sec. 7.b).
When the heading could take --Excerpts, use the free-floating subdivision --Excerpts, Arranged instead (sec. 7.c).

entries.rule: Used instead of the qualifier , Arranged when the heading could be modified by --Excerpts (cf. H 1160).

entries.pattern: [Sacred songs|Solo cantatas|Solo cantatas, Sacred|Solo cantatas, Secular|Songs|Vocalises] ([High voice|Medium voice|Low voice])
entries.rule: One solo voice: vocal range qualifier is the first element in parentheses after the main heading. These headings have been established with each range qualifier.
exceptions: No range qualifier with Vocal duets ... Vocal nonets or Sacred vocal duets ... Sacred vocal nonets (sec. 8.a(2)).

entries.rule: Established headings for 2 through 9 solo voices; no indication of range.
Number of solo voices (two or more) added on a free-floating basis; no voice range.

One solo voice in a heading that does not state or imply medium: qualifier begins with Voice; order sung part(s), solo instrument, accompaniment; no vocal range, no nature of text. A second heading may be added.
examples: Sacred monologues with music (Voice with orchestra)
exceptions: Do not add , Unaccompanied when voice is the sole medium (sec. 8.b(3)).

entries.rule: Two or more solo voices: arabic numeral in parentheses after Voices; up to 9; no authority records required.
examples: Monologues with music (Voices (2), oboe, trumpet with orchestra)
exceptions: Do not add , Unaccompanied when voice is the sole medium: Canons, fugues, etc. (Voices (3)) (sec. 8.b(3)).

entries.rule: Qualifiers for type of voices are free-floating after these three headings.

entries.pattern: [Cantatas|Cantatas, Sacred|Cantatas, Secular|Masses|Requiems] ([type of chorus other than Mixed voices])
entries.rule: Mixed voices is assumed and never added; other chorus types have been established with these headings.
exceptions: Cantatas (Mixed voices), Masses (Mixed voices), etc. are not used: Cantatas; Cantatas, Sacred; Cantatas, Secular; Masses; Requiems.

entries.rule: Number of choral parts (8 or fewer) follows type of chorus after a comma in the same parentheses; only with these three headings and only if accompaniment is not present in the heading, is for continuo, for a solo instrument, or for two of the same keyboard instruments, or with , Unaccompanied. Divisi not counted separately unless throughout most or all of the vocal line.
examples: Choruses, Sacred (Mixed voices, 6 parts) with continuo
Choruses, Sacred (Mixed voices, 4 parts) with piano
Choruses, Secular (Women's voices, 3 parts) with harp
exceptions: Not with ensemble accompaniment.
Not more than 8 parts.
Not with headings other than Choruses; Choruses, Sacred; Choruses, Secular.

entries.rule: Qualifier begins with Chorus; order sung part(s), solo instrument, accompaniment; no type of chorus, no nature of text. A second heading may be added.
examples: Canons, fugues, etc. (Chorus and trumpet with string orchestra)
Symphonies (Chorus and viola with chamber orchestra)
Canons, fugues, etc. (Chorus with instrumental ensemble)
exceptions: Do not use , Unaccompanied when chorus is the only medium of performance.

entries.pattern: [vocal heading with qualifier] with [single instrument | two of the same keyboard instrument ([Instruments] (2)) | ensemble]
entries.rule: Accompaniment is the last element. Name a specific instrument only for one instrument or two of the same keyboard instrument; otherwise use the ensemble term. Keyboard hands in comma form: with piano, 4 hands.
examples: Choruses, Sacred (Mixed voices) with keyboard ensemble
Choruses, Sacred (Mixed voices) with brass ensemble
exceptions: not Choruses, Sacred (Mixed voices) with organ and piano
not Songs (High voice) with string quartet
not Songs (Medium voice) with piano trio
not Choruses, Sacred (Mixed voices) with brass trio
not Canons, fugues, etc. (Chorus and trumpet with organ)
No accompaniment added to larger vocal forms and dramatic works: Cantatas; Masses; Musicals; Operas; Oratorios; Requiems; Sacred pantomimes with music; Solo cantatas (sec. 10.a).

entries.rule: Final element; free-floating with Choruses; Choruses, Sacred; Choruses, Secular; Sacred vocal duets, [trios, etc.]; Sacred songs; Songs; Vocal duets [trios, etc.]; Vocalises — including when modified by range of solo voice or type of chorus.
exceptions: Authority record required with Masses; Requiems (including with type of chorus); Sacred vocal ensembles; Vocal ensembles, e.g. Masses, Unaccompanied; Requiems (Women's voices), Unaccompanied (sec. 11.a(2)).
Not with (Voice ...)/(Voices ...) qualifier headings where voice is the sole medium (sec. 8.b(3)) or (Chorus ...) qualifier headings (sec. 9.b).
Not with the sec. 10.a headings (Cantatas; Musicals; Operas; Oratorios; Sacred pantomimes with music; Solo cantatas), except Masses and Requiems by authority record.
Never in headings for instrumental music (sec. 11.b).

ordering_groups.group: plucked or hammered stringed instruments without a keyboard

ordering_groups.within_group_order: score order, high to low, basing the order on the range of each instrument as described in standard music reference sources

ordering_notes: Do not include more than 9 instruments or 9 soloists in a heading, counting all categories.

For two instruments (Western music on Western instruments; optionally one Western and one non-Western): if one is chordal (keyboard or plucked instruments, on which chords are easily played) or accompanies the other, give the chordal or accompanying instrument in the second position.
Group assignments below are as stated or as implied by the sheet's examples; the sheet does not itself tabulate instruments by group.

sec. 1.a(3); only for works for one or two solo players, otherwise "flute"
sec. 1.a(3); only for works for one or two solo players, otherwise "trombone"
sec. 2 (Octets example: after mandolin, before percussion); sec. 5.b(3) Accordion ensembles
sec. 2 (Pianos (2), celesta, percussion, synthesizer ...); sec. 4.b(4)(a) treats celesta with mallet instruments
sec. 2, 4.b(5), 5.d; never numbered; music heading is Electronic music, combination form "electronic" (Electronic and percussion music, Balloon and electronic music)
sec. 1.a(4) (Leaf music; Leaves (Musical medium of performance))

large_ensembles_more_than_one_player_to_.note: The word "ensembles" is not part of headings in this category.

terms.note: appears only as medium in examples

ensembles_one_player_to_a_part.note: For individual works "ensemble(s)" stands for 10 or more instruments, except as indicated in sec. 5.b(3)-(6); in collections it may represent varying instrumentation or numbers of players. Main heading plural; medium singular.

terms.note: as in Choruses, Sacred (Mixed voices) with keyboard ensemble

percussion_ensembles.note: Stands for two or more performers, each playing one or more instruments, in works solely for percussion or where the accompaniment is solely for percussion.

jazz_ensemble.note: Not used as a main heading (see Jazz); used only as a medium of performance for a group of two or more solo instruments with other accompaniment, or for the accompanying group itself.

sung_part_medium_terms.use: one solo voice in a heading not stating/implying medium (sec. 8.b(1))
chorus in a heading not stating/implying medium (sec. 9.b)

connectors.use: between exactly two solo instruments, or a sung part and one solo instrument in a qualifier; not when three or more elements precede "with" or more than two soloists (use commas)
precedes accompanying solo instrument(s) or accompanying ensemble

qualifiers.free_floating_with: form/genre headings for arranged instrumental music

number_modifiers.after: plural instrument name or Voices / Unspecified instruments
instrument as sole qualifier content, or keyboard accompaniment in vocal headings
number_modifiers.example: Sonatas (Viola, 3 hands); Songs (High voice) with piano, 4 hands
